svg.aria-label: Schematic comparison of three glucose polymers, each glucose unit drawn as a circle. Left, starch amylose: an unbranched chain of glucose joined by alpha 1,4 links that coils into a helix, about six glucose units per turn; digested by amylase. Middle, glycogen: a highly branched tree; straight runs are alpha 1,4 chains and each branch starts at an alpha 1,6 link, one branch point circled, with a branch about every 8 to 12 units; the many chain ends are shaded green because glucose is added or removed there. Right, cellulose: three straight, parallel chains of glucose joined by beta 1,4 links, with each unit flipped relative to its neighbor, and rows of dotted blue hydrogen bonds holding neighboring chains together in a sheet; humans cannot digest it.
